# Audio fixtures

Tiny test files for `atomik-audio-file`. Every file is 0.1 s (4410 frames) at 44.1 kHz and
under 40 KB (the largest, `stereo_wavf32.wav`, is 35 360 bytes). They are shorter than the
0.25 s first planned because 0.25 s of stereo 32-bit float is 88 KB.

All fixtures are synthetic: the sines are generated by the crate's own test and the other formats are encodings of those sines, so they contain no third-party audio. They are released under CC0 (public domain).

Signal: `stereo_*` has a 440 Hz sine (amplitude 0.5) on the left and a 660 Hz sine (amplitude
0.25) on the right. `mono_*` is the 440 Hz sine alone.

## Source files (written by the crate's own tests, not by ffmpeg)

`stereo_wav16.wav` and `mono_wav16.wav` are 16-bit PCM written with `hound`. They are the
ground truth: every lossless fixture must decode bit-exactly to `i16 / 32768`, and the tests read
the expected samples from these two files.

```
cargo test -p atomik-audio-file --test gen_fixtures -- --ignored
```

## Derived files (ffmpeg)

Run in this directory with ffmpeg 8.x (libmp3lame and libvorbis builds). `-map_metadata -1` and
`-bitexact` keep the output free of encoder tags and timestamps, so a rerun gives the same bytes.

```sh
for k in stereo mono; do
  O="-map_metadata -1 -fflags +bitexact -flags:a +bitexact"
  ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -y -i ${k}_wav16.wav $O -c:a pcm_s24le ${k}_wav24.wav
  ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -y -i ${k}_wav16.wav $O -c:a pcm_f32le ${k}_wavf32.wav
  ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -y -i ${k}_wav16.wav $O -c:a pcm_s16be -f aiff ${k}_aiff16.aif
  ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -y -i ${k}_wav16.wav $O -c:a flac -sample_fmt s16 ${k}_flac.flac
  ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -y -i ${k}_wav16.wav $O -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 128k -write_id3v2 0 ${k}_mp3.mp3
  ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -y -i ${k}_wav16.wav $O -c:a libvorbis -q:a 4 ${k}_ogg.ogg
done
```

| File suffix | Format | Decoded exactly? |
|---|---|---|
| `_wav16.wav` | 16-bit PCM WAV | yes |
| `_wav24.wav` | 24-bit PCM WAV | yes (`i16 << 8` over `2^23` equals `i16 / 2^15`) |
| `_wavf32.wav` | 32-bit float WAV | yes |
| `_aiff16.aif` | 16-bit PCM AIFF (big-endian) | yes |
| `_flac.flac` | 16-bit FLAC | yes |
| `_mp3.mp3` | MP3, 128 kb/s CBR, LAME | no: frequency and RMS (1 dB) are tested |
| `_ogg.ogg` | Ogg Vorbis, quality 4 | no: frequency and RMS (1 dB) are tested |

Encoder padding: MP3 and Vorbis encoders prepend priming samples. These files carry gapless
information (the LAME/Xing header, the Ogg granule positions), which symphonia applies, so they
decode to exactly 4410 frames. The tests still allow up to 2 MP3 frames (2304) of extra length,
and measure level and pitch only over the middle half of the clip, so a decoder that does not
trim padding passes too.
